correctness.rationale: This PASS is for /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md, not for the uncorrected derivation. Frozen lines 34 and 57 use br−aq=1 for a/q<b/r, which is false, for example for the first pair 0/1<1/n. The repair uses bq−ar=1 and supplies a direct proof of the critical no-other-speed interference assertion: write (p,k)=u(a,q)+v(b,r) in the unimodular basis of neighboring Farey vectors. Because 0<k≤n<q+r, exactly one coefficient is positive and the other is nonpositive. On the gap this gives |kt−p| at least the minimum of the two endpoint distances qt−a, b−rt; the endpoint vectors themselves realize the candidates. Thus the gap length under the common strict threshold is exactly the positive-part summand, for every nonnegative threshold. The ordered denominator reconstruction handles each wrap endpoint without duplication. All slope jumps are positive, and the odd-sum, even-m, and odd-m constructions exhaust attainable coprime sums except 2n−2 for even n; n=2 merely omits an index outside the range. At 1/(2n) there is no clipping, each center contributes twice to the slope sum, and Möbius inversion gives the totient limit. For the final segment only q+r=n+1 has positive length; the reciprocal partial fractions and reduced mediants yield the harmonic sum, separate open components, and the distinct points only in the non-strict critical set. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed. Independently subdividing the circle at exact rational events and testing intervening midpoints matched 143 measures for 2≤n≤14 and all 13 critical point sets in that range (python3 /workspace/review_checks.py); the proof gives the full domain.
